core_obligations: Show that for f : X to Y proper with both locally of finite type over a discrete valuation ring R, the square with specialization maps sp_{X/R}, sp_{Y/R} horizontally and proper pushforward vertically commutes (proof lines 556-582). First, by the construction of the specialization map, sp_{X/R}([Z_K]) = [Z_kappa]_r for an integral closed subscheme Z of X dominating R, and this characterizes the map; for Z' = f(Z), an integral closed subscheme of Y dominating R, likewise sp_{Y/R}([Z'_K]) = [Z'_kappa]_r (proof lines 557-561). Second, view [Z] in Z_{r+1}(X); by definition of proper pushforward on cycles, f_*[Z] = 0 if dim(Z') < r+1 and f_*[Z] = d[Z'] if Z to Z' is generically finite of degree d; by chow-lemma-flat-pullback-proper-pushforward (tag 02RG) proper pushforward commutes with flat pullback by Y_K to Y, so correspondingly f_{K,*}[Z_K] = 0 or d[Z'_K] (proof lines 564-569). Third, apply chow-lemma-closed-in-X-gysin (tag 02TA) to the commutative diagram of closed fibres X_kappa over Y_kappa inside X over Y, obtaining f_{kappa,*}[Z_kappa]_r = 0 or d[Z'_kappa]_r, since clearly the Gysin maps give i^*[Z] = [Z_kappa]_r and j^*[Z'] = [Z'_kappa]_r for cycles not contained in the closed fibres (proof lines 570-580). Combining, sp_{Y/R}(f_{K,*}[Z_K]) = f_{kappa,*}(sp_{X/R}([Z_K])) in both cases, and since the [Z_K] generate Z_r(X_K) the square commutes (proof lines 581).
proof_roadmap: Characterize both composite maps on generators via the defining property of the specialization map on integral subschemes dominating R (proof lines 557-561).
Dichotomy for the pushforward of the whole subscheme and transport to the generic fibres by commutation with flat pullback (proof lines 564-569).
Transport to the closed fibres by the Gysin base-change lemma and match the two composites on generators (proof lines 570-581).
